subject: Proposal: consolidate two runtime IC roles into one Senior Platform Engineer
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: consolidate two runtime IC roles into one Senior Platform Engineer

Team —

TL;DR: I recommend we convert the two currently-open Runtime IC requisitions (R-7842, R-7843) into a single Senior Platform Engineer role focused on runtime kernel + serving optimizations. The goal is to reduce near-term headcount pressure while keeping the delivery plan for Q4 latency improvements intact.

Why:
- Work profile overlap: both reqs target low-level runtime/kernels work with ~50% of the same responsibilities (kernel tuning, batching logic, runtime observability).
- Hiring market: senior candidates with both kernel and systems experience are scarce; a consolidated senior hire yields faster ramp and higher impact.
- Cost: one senior band (L6+) with targeted comp package is ~15–20% cheaper than two mid-level hires (L4/L5) once onboarding and ramp are considered.

Ask:
1) Approval to close R-7843 and re-open a single Senior Platform Engineer (R-7921) in FY28 headcount plan.
2) Sign-off on proposed comp band in attached comp-band-table.xlsx (I recommend band L6, base band midpoint with a slightly higher equity target for a critical hire).
3) Temporary approval to engage BrightBridge Talent for an accelerated search; they have a shortlist for senior runtime/platform candidates (sample: Lucas Zhao).

Attachments: hc_bizcase_20280625.pdf (business case), comp-band-table.xlsx
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4platform-hc-bizcase

Notes: If we get approval this week I can instruct TA to pause postings for the two separate reqs and move the budget/req code to the single role. This avoids double-spend in the run-rate.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Proposal: consolidate two runtime IC roles into one Senior Platform Engineer

Irene —

Thanks for the write-up and attachments. A few quick items I need before I can greenlight the consolidation:

1) Headcount accounting: confirm which req ID we retire and where the remaining FTE budget tracks (we need the org code for cost center alignment).
2) Delta to FY28 run-rate if we swap two L4/L5 hires for one L6 — please give 12-month run-rate number (salary + benefits + ramp cost).
3) Impact to deliverables: outline any tasks that would be deprioritized or delayed if we reduce the slot count (quick list in the biz case doc would be enough).

If those are in the biz case already point me to the exact sections; otherwise can you add a one-pager with the three bullets above? I can accelerate review after that.

Also cc'ing Neha for hiring-side sequencing.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
SVP, Finance & Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: consolidate two runtime IC roles into one Senior Platform Engineer

Kimberly / Irene —

Short answers inline to make the review quicker: 

1) Headcount accounting: retire R-7843 and reassign budget to new req R-7921. Cost center will remain INFRA-PLATFORM-2 (same as the two original reqs). I’ll update the HR slate once we have sign-off.

2) Delta to run-rate: rough numbers (rounded):
- Two mid-level (L4/L5) hires: total comp fully loaded year 1 = $540k
- One senior (L6) hire: total comp fully loaded year 1 = $440k
=> 12-month run-rate reduction ≈ $100k.
These are estimates — Kimberly, please flag if you want finance to model with exact benefit load.

3) Deliverables impact:
- What changes: longer tail on lower-priority kernel experiments (we’ll prioritize hot-path latency wins and critical batching fixes).
- What stays: serving runtime SLO improvements targeted for Q4 (core work covered).
- Risk: single point of failure for cross-squad coverage; mitigation: rotate a senior SWE from kernel team for 20% time during first 3 months.

I support the consolidation if Finance is comfortable with the delta. This gives us more runway and a higher-seniority hire that can own the kernel roadmap end-to-end.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference
